12467.title: C
12467.content: Categorize and summarize candidate, extracted Each hit gets a category (overlaps: coordinate; affected by; out of scope; unrelated) and a one-line summary with its state. Judgement, not a keyword score: say why each is in its category. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/related-work.bpmn#A_Categorize . Check before you create (exact-title search) candidate, extracted STRICT. beans create is not idempotent: it mints a fresh id every call and dedupes on nothing, so re-entering a step duplicates the plan instead of no-op'ing. In the qou folio an unguarded re-run produced 14,688 duplicate beans — 92% of every open bean — which starved the idle-backlog policy of signal and collided with 15 real ids. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/bean-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_CheckExists . Check it candidate, extracted Look, do not remember. The answer is one of the four states, and "could not determine" is its own answer: a check that could not look is not a pass. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/complete-initialization.bpmn#A_CheckStep . Check staleness (source hash) candidate, extracted On source content change: computes sha256(source.md) and compares to each translation's status.json sourceHash. If they differ, sets stale: true. The translation remains visible with a "stale — needs re-adjudication" indicator. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/translation-workflow.bpmn#Task_StalenessCheck . Check the base AST against the IG's inputs [ig-ast-delta] candidate, extracted ig-ast.ts validity <base> --ig <root>: folio-assistant-core's compiledValidity on the manifest's inputs, with the input digest recomputed by the same algorithm as the Java writer. Exit 0 valid, 1 stale-inputs (names which input), 2 cannot-tell. Run against the BASE revision's checkout. BPMN activities of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/processes/content/ig-ast-delta-review.bpmn#Task_Validity . Check the JSON Schemas and JSON-LD are at their IRIs candidate, extracted THE PRIMARY STEP of initializing a Knowledge Graph harness (owner, 2026-09-30: "json(ld) is primary step in initializing KG harness"), and so the first one checked once the declarations are read. Every JSON Schema the harness publishes (its $id) and every JSON-LD document (its vocabulary, its diagram vocabulary, its graph export, each carrying its own @context) is at the address it names under iriBase, where a program following the IRI finds it. Two checks: that the site build stages each one at its address, and that each address answers. A 404 is not published; a 403 or no answer from here could not be determined. The Pages site is the vehicle: when the documents are not yet answering, the site steps below are how they get there, and the report leads with this step's state. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/complete-initialization.bpmn#A_CheckDocuments . Check the selected methodology's evidence base candidate, extracted Before applying a methodology, establish that the thing being applied is what it claims to be. A methodology is adopted because it is somebody else's named, external work; this step checks that the origin it cites resolves to a source in a declared library, and reads the methodology-evidence QA sidecar for it. WHY THE CHECK IS HERE AND NOT AT ADOPTION. Adoption happens once; selection happens every time a decision is made. A source that was reachable when the methodology was adopted can stop being so, and a methodology adopted before this axis existed was never checked at all. Measured 2026-09-22: six methodologies cited an origin and NONE had that source in any library, so every selection made until then rested on an unverifiable citation. WHAT A GAP DOES AND DOES NOT DO. A missing source does NOT block the decision, and this step has no branch that stops the process — that would make a documentation gap into an outage, and the owner decides whether an unbacked methodology may still be used. It does two things: it runs literature-search to try to close the gap, and it puts the evidence state into the record A_Record writes, so a reader can tell a decision made on a verified method from one made on a citation nobody could follow. The third state is the one that matters. "Source ingested", "source located but unreachable from here" and "no source found" are three different facts, and literature-search exists largely to stop the middle one being reported as the last. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/options-analysis.bpmn#A_CheckEvidence . Check the slug's SHAPE and that the confirmation repeats it candidate, extracted Guarded three ways because a dispatch input is a DELETION TRIGGER. workflow_dispatch is available only to an actor with write access; the slug must match exactly the characters the sed pipeline can produce, with . and .. refused by name; and the confirmation must repeat the slug, so a confirmation cannot be carried over from an earlier run against a different preview. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/feature-staging.bpmn#Task_Validate . Check translation completeness candidate, extracted Verify that all msgid entries have msgstr translations. Partial translations are acceptable for initial submissions but must be flagged for follow-up. The coordinator checks: - % of strings translated - Any fuzzy-flagged entries - Missing critical sections . BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/human-translation-workflow.bpmn#Task_CheckCompleteness . Check what is served candidate, extracted Ask the root URL and every document address. 2xx or 3xx answers; 404 is not there; 403, 407, 5xx or no answer is about the way here and could not be determined. BPMN activities of bootstrap-tools · source bootstrap-tools/processes/render-kg-to-github-pages.bpmn#A_CheckServed . Check what was staged candidate, extracted site.ts --check and readme-book.ts --check: every document at its address, no address taken by another file, every link on the page landing. This is the QA of what would be pushed. BPMN activities of bootstrap-tools · source bootstrap-tools/processes/render-kg-to-github-pages.bpmn#A_CheckStaged . Choose a candidate candidate, extracted A one-off choice between surviving candidates. Rejected candidates are kept, with the reason each lost. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/ui/wireframe-design-review.bpmn#Call_Choose . Choose a destination, or none candidate, extracted A PERSON'S STEP, and none is one of the answers rather than a refusal to answer. A requirement whose whole content is carried by the code becomes a commit and nothing else; a graph that acquires a node for it is a graph with a node nobody will ever read. The default creates NOTHING. An agent that decides on its own that a requirement "is really a skill" has manufactured a node nobody asked for, in a graph somebody else maintains — which is what this step exists to prevent. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-signoff.bpmn#BA_ChooseKg . Choose from the offered options candidate, extracted The question is presented as a short list of selectable options, never as free prose, and the list names the top-level content types the agent knows about. The answer becomes the statedIntent fact and the table is evaluated again — the user's answer is read as evidence, like any other fact. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/conduct/getting-started.bpmn#Task_AskIntent . Choose subgraphs, the asset policy, harnesses candidate, extracted Written to the entry as subgraphs, assets.policy (none, on-demand or all) and harnesses. Choosing is not holding: a chosen subgraph is still referenced until the gates below let it through. Choosing nothing is legitimate — a subscription with no parts chosen is a pinned reference, the case associatedHarnesses covers today. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/subscribe-kg.bpmn#Task_Choose . Circulate the draft [content-review] candidate, extracted The draft publication is circulated to the review team for formal review. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/draft-to-publication.bpmn#Task_CirculateDraft . Cite the author of every narrative candidate, extracted A generated description is a claim by someone. Record whether a human or an agent wrote it, and for an agent the model version. An uncited narrative is indistinguishable from a transcription of the source. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/ingest-derive-content.bpmn#Task_Provenance . Claim it (status: in-progress) candidate, extracted Idempotent. Claim BEFORE working, and note the branch, so a sibling session can see the item is taken rather than discovering it by collision. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/bean-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_Claim . Claim or open the bean [todo-manager] candidate, extracted Every edit is tracked as a bean in beans/. Check for an existing bean by exact title first; claim it (status in-progress) rather than minting a duplicate. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/editing-hci-validation.bpmn#Task_ClaimBean . Claim the work item candidate, extracted Claim before you work. A claim ANNOUNCES rather than reserves until the PR exists, which is why the branch is announced at the next step and not at the end. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/code-change-review.bpmn#Task_ClaimBean . Classify every conflicted path against the declared patterns candidate, extracted The first matching pattern decides: take-base, generated-regions, qa-sidecar, or refuse. A path no pattern names refuses. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/merge-base.bpmn#Task_Classify . Classify what changed candidate, extracted Prose, code nodes, or both. This is the only decision the generic lane makes on its own: everything after it is made inside a subprocess by the role that lane binds. Binds content-review, the same skill as Task_Consolidate in this lane, since placement PR3 (bean 63wl): it named semantic-review-scoping, a paper skill folio-assistant-sci owns, which this harness diagram cannot reach. A paper process that wants semantic scoping adds it by calling this process. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/content/review-task.bpmn#Task_ClassifyChange . Clinical / scientific sign-off [content-review] candidate, extracted Domain sign-off: clinical SMEs for a guideline, subject-matter reviewers for a paper. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/draft-to-publication.bpmn#Task_SmeSignoff . Clinical validation [content-review] candidate, extracted Ground truth: does the DAK say what the guideline says? . BPMN activities of smart-base · source smart-base/processes/content/l2-dak-authoring.bpmn#Task_SmeValidate . Close issue ONLY on BA authorisation candidate, extracted Reachable only through BA_Confirm, which is the BA saying every criterion is met. An agent must never close an issue without that explicit authorisation — the gate is the preceding task, and this name says so rather than leaving a reader to trace the flow for it. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-close.bpmn#A_Close . Close the bean, merge commit as evidence candidate, extracted The asset carries no description. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/merge-refusal.bpmn#Task_Close . Close the publication manager's alert, if open candidate, extracted A clean publish resolves whatever the last failure raised: close the open publication-manager tracking issue with a comment naming this run. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/docs-site-publish.bpmn#Task_CloseAlert . Close the release beans [todo-manager] candidate, extracted What shipped is resolved; what slipped stays open and carries into the next cycle. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/draft-to-publication.bpmn#Task_CloseReleaseBeans . Close the session candidate, extracted Records that the actor stopped. It does NOT resolve beans or complete instances: those outlive the session by design, and a machine that closed them on the way out would be asserting work finished because somebody went away. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/session-state-machine.bpmn#A_CloseSession . Close the tracking issue candidate, extracted Clean: close the open ci-health issue, if any, saying why (main is clean). Runs only on a clean verdict — on unknown the issue is left untouched and the job fails instead, because could-not-check is never rendered as clean. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/ci-health-watch.bpmn#Task_Close . Close the tracking issue candidate, extracted Clean: close the open pr-no-checks issue, if any, saying why (every open pull request's head now has a CI run). Runs only on a clean verdict — on unknown the issue is left untouched and the job fails instead, because could-not-check is never rendered as clean. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/pr-checks-present.bpmn#Task_Close . Close the tracking issue candidate, extracted Clean: close the open repo-health issue, if any, saying why (every check ran and none had anything to report). Runs only on a clean verdict — on unknown the issue is left untouched and the job fails instead, because could-not-check is never rendered as clean. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/repository-health-watch.bpmn#Task_Close . Close the tracking issue candidate, extracted Closed automatically when every pin is current, so the issue's existence is the state rather than a log of past states. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/upstream-pin-watch.bpmn#Task_CloseIssue . Close the window back to its avatar candidate, extracted [x] closes the window back to its avatar. Only a person's [x] does this; a zoom-out never closes a window, or [x] and zooming become indistinguishable to the reader. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/ui/board-open-close.bpmn#A_Close . Close-out candidate, extracted The stakeholders sign off, the BA confirms every criterion is met, and only then does the agent close the issue. Never the other way round: an agent must never assume completion. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-requirements.bpmn#Call_Close . Code node review candidate, extracted Descend into Process_CodeReview. The actor takes on the code-reviewer lane for this call path only. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/content/review-task.bpmn#Call_CodeReview . Collate findings into a report candidate, extracted Mechanical results and review findings are merged into one report against the proposed change. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/editing-hci-validation.bpmn#Task_CollateFindings . Collect or reconstruct a handover report per agent candidate, extracted Use the agent's own report and check it against live state; if none, ask the agent if it is still reachable, else reconstruct with the handover-report template and mark it reconstructed. Unpushed state is unknown, never empty. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/stalled-agent-triage.bpmn#A_Collect . Comment on the open issue, naming the step candidate, extracted Add this failure to the open issue as a comment (which notifies), and refresh the body to the latest state. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/publish-alert.bpmn#A_Comment . Comment on the PR once, linking the bean candidate, extracted One comment per refused PR, edited in place on every later event. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/merge-refusal.bpmn#Task_Comment . Comment ONCE per (PR, head sha) candidate, extracted Comment on each affected open PR once per (PR, head sha): a hidden marker carrying the sha is checked first, so a re-run on the same head stays silent and a new push can be reported again. A PR that is no longer open is skipped. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/pr-checks-present.bpmn#Task_Comment . Comment staging URL on PR candidate, extracted Bot comments or updates the staging URL on the PR. Includes commit SHA, branch name, and build log link. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/content-change-review.bpmn#Task_CommentPR . Comment the preview URL on the PR candidate, extracted Post, or update in place, one comment on the PR giving the preview URL (STAGING/<slug>/) and the commit it was built from. Pull-request events only. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/feature-staging.bpmn#Task_Comment . Commit a tip without the pruned entries candidate, extracted One new commit whose tree lacks the pruned entries, parented on the current tip, through the same fetch → rebuild → push loop as a publish: no -f, three attempts. History is not rewritten — truncating it is a deletion of a different order and the owner's call (deletion-requires-confirmation), not a scheduled job's. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/qa-publish.bpmn#Task_ApplyPrune . Commit into the corpus candidate, extracted Only now does the change become corpus content, together with its QA sidecars. Subject to the commit-hygiene requirement. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/editing-hci-validation.bpmn#Task_Commit . Commit the merge candidate, extracted The asset carries no description. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/merge-base.bpmn#Task_Commit . Commit, push, open the PR candidate, extracted The PR opens at the FIRST commit, even on a stub, and permission is never asked for it. Holding a green PR back for someone to look at is not caution — it is a blocked reviewer. A change to a rendered surface carries a before/after preview in the PR body (skill before-after-preview). BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/code-change-review.bpmn#Task_CommitAndOpenPR . Commit, push, update PR candidate, extracted Agent commits all changes to the feature branch and pushes. The feature-staging.yml workflow automatically deploys to STAGING/<branch-slug>/ and comments the URL on the PR. For a rendered change the agent also produces the before/after preview (skill before-after-preview) and links it in the PR body. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/content-change-review.bpmn#Task_CommitPush . Compare main vs staging candidate, extracted Review committee opens both URLs side by side: - Main site: <pages-url>/ (current published state) - Staging: <pages-url>/STAGING/<branch-slug>/ The staging banner shows the commit SHA so they can verify what they are reviewing matches the PR. A changed figure, diagram or table is also pictured before and after on the review page, with the share of changed pixels in words (skill visual-diff, Tool folio-block-screenshots). Anything the staging job cannot picture (page chrome, scroll behaviour, a PDF page, an IG page) is in the agent's before/after preview (skill before-after-preview). BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/content-change-review.bpmn#Task_CompareBeforeAfter . Complete (no unchecked todos left) candidate, extracted Only once nothing is unchecked, and with a summary of what changed. The engine's resolve completes a bean only after the instance itself has completed — whether work is done is a judgement, and a bean is not closed on someone else's say-so. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/bean-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_Complete . Compose the message candidate, extracted Five required strings — timestamp, actor, process, task, message — and one optional markdown body. The five are required because each answers a question a reader of the log will otherwise have to guess, and a guessed answer in a log is worse than a missing one. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/log-message.bpmn#A_Compose . Compute the cone of the change (fsh-cone --changed) candidate, extracted content/pipeline/fsh-cone.ts over the changed files: the forward cone is what to rebuild, the backward cone is what to check out. BPMN activities of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/processes/content/ig-incremental-build.bpmn#Task_Cone . Confirm all criteria met candidate, extracted The business analyst confirms every acceptance criterion from the requirements is met. The issue closes only on their authorisation — an agent never closes an issue on its own say-so. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-close.bpmn#BA_Confirm . Confirm needs statement candidate, extracted Stakeholders confirm, on the issue, that the needs statement says what they need — or say what to change. A stakeholder's judgement; an agent does not record it for them. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-needs.bpmn#S_ConfirmNeeds . Confirm the cardinalities candidate, extracted An operational question, asked of the people who run the process because they know where the exceptions are. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-data-model.bpmn#S_ConfirmCardinality . Confirm the entities are the ones meant candidate, extracted A naming question. The BA owns the domain vocabulary; the agent does not guess, which is CRDM's own rule for phase 1 and applies here with more force. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-data-model.bpmn#BA_ConfirmEntities . Consolidate findings candidate, extracted One report from however many subprocesses ran. Findings are advice: a reviewer cannot accept the change. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/content/review-task.bpmn#Task_Consolidate . Consolidate into 2-4 themes, with a recommendation each candidate, extracted Group by what the work delivers, not by agent. Each theme gets its epic, members, dependencies, risk, and one of: continue, fold in, new epic, park, scrap (owner only). BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/stalled-agent-triage.bpmn#A_Consolidate . Coordinate? How? candidate, extracted The asset carries no description. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/related-work.bpmn#U_Coordinate . COPYRIGHT per bitstream, and for the derived work candidate, extracted What the licence permits for THIS bitstream, and separately whether it permits the derivation. LICENSE-CONTENT.md exists in this repository and the ingestion pipeline does not read it. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/materialize-remote.bpmn#Task_Copyright . Create feature branch candidate, extracted Agent creates a feature branch from main. Branch naming: feature/<short-description> Opens a PR immediately (AGENTS.md: "open the PR at the first commit"). BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/content-change-review.bpmn#Task_CreateBranch . Create the bean (agent CLI, not an engine op) candidate, extracted beans create "<title>". This is the AGENT's call. The workflow engine has no create op — its vocabulary is claim, note and resolve, all of which act on an instance's existing bean. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/bean-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_Create . Create the repositories candidate, extracted The owner creates the content and tools repositories and their Pages. Nothing is committed to them before this. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-separation.bpmn#Task_Create . Create the repository candidate, extracted Only on the new-repo branch, and only after the user has named it. An empty working directory is scaffolded in place instead. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/conduct/getting-started.bpmn#Task_CreateRepo . Cross the axes into SO, WO, ST, WT candidate, extracted The TOWS matching step, and the only step that produces anything actionable. Strengths and weaknesses across, opportunities and threats down, and each cell names the strategy the pairing implies: SO — achieve opportunities that greatly match the strengths; WO — overcome weaknesses to attain opportunities; ST — use strengths to reduce vulnerability to threats; WT — prevent weaknesses, to avoid becoming more susceptible to threats. A SWOT that stops at four lists is the failure the source names as its central one. This step is what the process exists to reach. It produces CANDIDATE strategies, not a chosen one, and they are not ranked — see the process documentation on why no scoring activity exists. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/swot-analysis.bpmn#A_Cross . Cut the subgraph that leaves candidate, extracted Apply the editorial scope mechanically and report what it removed. A selection that reports nothing cannot be told from one that ran over an empty rule. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-to-portal.bpmn#A_Select .

12468.content: Data dictionary and core data elements [l2-dak-authoring] candidate, extracted Author the data dictionary and core data elements for this component. Stay structured but not FHIR: a data element a clinician can review, from which L3 can later be derived rather than written twice. BPMN activities of smart-base · source smart-base/processes/content/l2-dak-authoring.bpmn#Task_DataDict . Data model Entities + cardinalities candidate, extracted Between requirements and sign-off, and the order is the argument: requirements are statements about things, and the model says what the things ARE. Drafted earlier it is invented from nothing, since the entities come from the phase-2 BPA; drafted later, sign-off approves requirements whose nouns were never pinned — which is how two stakeholders approve one sentence meaning different things. Owner, 2026-09-20. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-requirements.bpmn#Call_DataModel . Decide each theme candidate, extracted The asset carries no description. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/stalled-agent-triage.bpmn#U_Decide . Decide what may leave the repository candidate, extracted EDITORIAL, and it is stage 1 rather than a filter bolted to the exporter. kg-export produces the WHOLE graph because inspection wants the whole graph; a portal wants what its readers may see. Running the second as the first is how a QA verdict, a bean's blocking note or an unpublished draft reaches a public cache. Decided once, here, rather than at each consumer. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-to-portal.bpmn#E_Scope . Decide, weighing the recommendations candidate, extracted public-comment decide, or decide: code on GitHub from a login in config.json editors. accepted, accepted-modified, not-accepted, noted, deferred; a reason for all but accepted. Also reopens a decided comment. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/public-comment.bpmn#Task_EditorDecides . Decision logic · DMN tables [dmn-authoring] candidate, extracted Author the decision logic as DMN tables, within the FEEL subset the interpreter implements (any, literals, comparisons, one-of). Ranges, not() and function calls are refused at load, so write inside the subset. BPMN activities of smart-base · source smart-base/processes/content/l2-dak-authoring.bpmn#Task_Dmn . Declare the model where a tool can read it candidate, extracted A model in prose is a proposal; a model in the declaration is a model. Ship a reader in the same change — everything here that was only documentation went inert within weeks. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-data-model.bpmn#A_Declare . Declare the node materialized candidate, extracted The node's state moves from referenced to materialized, carrying purpose, localPath, gates and (archival) fixity. There is NO default state: a node that has not said is invalid, because 'the author did not say' and 'the author said they could not tell' are different facts. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/materialize-remote.bpmn#Task_Declare . Declare the purpose: working or archival candidate, extracted working or archival, and it is asked FIRST because three of the five gates mean different things under each. An archival copy keeps the original bytes, never expires, requires fixity, and is the only thing that discharges sourceLoss; a working copy keeps derived content and discharges none of that. A process that gated first and asked afterwards would be judging a copy whose obligations it did not yet know. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/materialize-remote.bpmn#Task_Purpose . Deduplicate, and keep what is actually relevant candidate, extracted The paper's Refiner. Accumulates into the evidence set the report is built from — so what is dropped here is invisible downstream, which is why it is a step somebody performs rather than a filter buried in retrieval. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/library/deep-document-research.bpmn#A_Refine . Deploy the MVP to staging candidate, extracted An MVP is shared AS A STAGING DEPLOY, not as a description of one. feature-staging.yml publishes the branch under STAGING/<branch-slug>/ on gh-pages and comments the URL on the PR, so the stakeholder who tests it is looking at the built artefact rather than at a screenshot — the same argument the merge discipline makes about rendered work. Measured in this repo on 2026-09-16: holding a rendered change back for assessment made assessment harder, not safer. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-deliver.bpmn#A_DeployStaging . Deploy the preview site [content-publish] candidate, extracted A preview never seeds the shared cache. BPMN activities of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/processes/content/ig-incremental-build.bpmn#Task_DeployPreview . Deploy the rendering candidate, extracted Commit the staged tree onto gh-pages as a full replace (the instance's Pages workflow on a push to main, or by hand); GitHub Pages then builds it from the branch. Rebuild and retry on a rejected push; never rebase the branch. The gh-pages commit SHA is the message the report names. BPMN activities of bootstrap-tools · source bootstrap-tools/processes/render-kg-to-github-pages.bpmn#A_Deploy . Deploy the site [content-publish] [ig-publication] candidate, extracted Deploy the site built from main or a release. Deploying is release-management, after a human authorised the release — an agent never records that authorisation. Report the published URL only once it answers: a returned deploy is not a serving site. BPMN activities of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/processes/content/ig-incremental-build.bpmn#Task_Deploy . Deploy to STAGING/<slug>/ candidate, extracted peaceiris/actions-gh-pages deploys to gh-pages branch under STAGING/<branch-slug>/ with keep_files: true so other staging deployments and the main site are preserved. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/content-change-review.bpmn#Task_DeployStaging . Derive content from the assets [document-intake] candidate, extracted See ingest-derive-content.bpmn. Most of this subprocess is not implemented yet. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/document-ingestion.bpmn#CallActivity_Derive . Derive the key [main/<sha> or pr/<n>/<sha>] candidate, extracted qa:publish --github reads the event: a push to main publishes under main/<sha>/, a pull request under pr/<n>/<head-sha>/ — the head that was tested, not the merge ref. It also reads whether the token can write, which the gateway after it routes on. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/qa-publish.bpmn#Task_DeriveKey . Derive the slug from the head ref candidate, extracted Derive the slug from the PR's head ref: every character outside [a-zA-Z0-9._-] becomes '-', runs of '-' collapse, and leading or trailing '-' is trimmed. It must be one safe path segment, checked by value. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/feature-staging.bpmn#Task_Slug . Describe the desired change candidate, extracted Author describes the content change in natural language. Example: "Update the immunization schedule to add a booster at 18 months." . BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/content-change-review.bpmn#Task_DescribeChange . Describe the intended change candidate, extracted The editor states the change in natural language; no content has moved yet. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/editing-hci-validation.bpmn#Task_DescribeChange . Describe the need (chat, issue, discussion) candidate, extracted The BA describes the capability gap in their own words. They do not need to know it is called CRDM. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-requirements.bpmn#BA_Submit . Detect change scope & impact candidate, extracted Agent analyses the requested change: - Which content blocks are affected? - Are there downstream implications (indicators, referral logic, visit schedules)? - Will deterministic logic (CQL/DMN) need updating? skill: content-graph, integration-watcher . BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/content-change-review.bpmn#Task_DetectScope . Detect feature request (crdm-detect skill) candidate, extracted Recognise the request as a platform capability change rather than content work, from crdm-detect's signals. Never call it "CRDM" to the person. Mid-content-work, ask whether to pause for requirements now or record a bean for later — do not switch on your own. If you are in no Process, that is an answer too: you are IDLE, and what you are doing is classifying a request to find the Process it belongs to — say that, rather than presenting a question as though a step had asked for it. So say which Role you are acting as — the lane of the CALLING task, since this lane is variable — and which Role the person you ask holds (the Requestor, or whoever the calling lane names). A broad question is answered from summaries and a specific one from chunks; a pipeline that picks once has answered every future question the same way. This checkout cannot yet offer the choice — l1-blocks.ts produces blocks, there is no summary level — so this step SAYS which granularity it searched rather than implying the corpus offered alternatives. 12471.title: G
12471.content: Gate every slice: slice:sqlite:check candidate, extracted For every slice: build twice and require one sha256; read the row digest back from the file and require it to equal the digest computed from the source without SQLite; run an FTS5 phrase query for a known row; and audit the payloads with auditPayloadTree (deploy payloads as written, the kg slice's pointers against the committed payload tree). A slice whose rows do not match its source fails; it never passes as whole. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/slice-sqlite-publish.bpmn#A_Check . Gather and verify the evidence [evidence-retrieval] candidate, extracted Before anything is drafted: the author reads the guidance ALREADY in this content, frames the question as PICO, retrieves candidates across the three evidence classes, and has each candidate's authority resolved against its publisher's own API. A recommendation reaches the drafting step with its evidence attached, or with the gap recorded. This step has nothing to do for content that carries no recommendations -- a mathematics folio has none -- and is skipped there rather than satisfied vacuously. Import hygiene (HARD) and advisories (WARN-ONLY) candidate, extracted FOUR QUESTIONS, ONE RUNNER — bean 7fu5. They were four jobs (lean-bare-import, python-imports, rust-wildcard, dependency-advisories), each about a second of work behind a ~13 s checkout and a runner request; measured on main run 37133247484 (2026-10-03), the run took 21.7 min while its longest job executed for 174 s, the rest waiting for runners. Now they are steps of the hygiene job, and every step after the first gate runs if: !cancelled(), so a red one masks none of the others — the om30 rule kept inside one job rather than by splitting it. (1) Lean, HARD: fail on any bare import Mathlib in content/**/*.lean; in this platform repo there is no content/, so the step prints SKIP and states that nothing was scanned. (2) Python, HARD: ruff F401 (unused) and F403 (wildcard) over the Python trees that exist, then the Python tests; an absent tree is dropped rather than passed to ruff, and an empty set says SKIP. (3) Dependency advisories, WARN-ONLY by the owner's ruling on bean j41m: is anything in the resolved tree KNOWN-VULNERABLE? The script exits 0 in every state and keeps them apart in its output; .github/dependabot.yml is the other half of that ruling and is not drawn here. (4) Rust wildcard imports, WARN-ONLY: report non-test use …::*; in tools/**/*.rs; continue-on-error, and therefore the job's LAST step, where it masks nothing. 12474.title: J
12474.content: Judge the assets in their design candidate, extracted A person looks at the ingested assets laid out in the design they are for, at BOTH a web and a mobile width. THIS IS A HUMAN STEP INSIDE INGESTION, and that is stated rather than hidden: ingest-theme.bpmn used to refuse to call this process for exactly that reason. The owner's ruling puts theme review at ingestion only, and a ruling that moves a review does not remove the person who performs it — so ingestion of a THEME SOURCE is attended at this step, while ingestion of everything else stays unattended because Gateway_ThemeSource routes it past. A judgement made at one viewport is incomplete, not passed, and the wireframe of the surface (wireframe-design-review) says what each layout was meant to be. Three defects in the landing board — a selector matching nothing, a crop cutting the subject, a fade wrong in both directions — were invisible to a clean build, a passing suite and every gate, and were found only by rendering the page and looking. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/ui/theme-ui-review.bpmn#R_Judge .

12475.title: K
12475.content: Keep it as a trial: the unpublished trashcan candidate, extracted A trial goes to the kept trashcan: addressable, exported, never published. Its node declares $schema: folio-fsh-guts/v1 and carries the bean or issue it was written under, since it was never moved from anywhere and a movedFrom would be invented provenance. It is NOT refreshed: a trial records what the source looked like when it was tried. Promoting a trial means running this process again with permanent = yes, so the gates are asked afresh. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/sample-import.bpmn#Task_Trial . Keep the local edit, and re-pin so it stops being asked candidate, extracted The local edit wins, so nothing is re-materialized — and the pin moves to the upstream revision that was compared against. Re-pinning is the half that is easy to forget and is the reason this is a step rather than an absence: without it the same upstream change is detected as new on every cycle, and a contributor is asked the same settled question for ever. The record says the copy is deliberately divergent FROM a named revision, which is a different claim from being stale against an unknown one. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/refresh-materialized.bpmn#Task_KeepLocal .

12477.content: Make sure every step is done candidate, extracted Following a harness's instructions once is not the same as every step being done. complete-initialization walks the steps the declarations name — FIRST the harness's JSON Schemas and JSON-LD at the IRIs they name, the primary step of initializing a Knowledge Graph harness; then declared directories, assets, the README and its sections, and the site that carries the documents — checks each, does what can be done, asks the person for what only they can do, and reports every step in its state. Options analysis accept · revise · discard candidate, extracted On the edge out of Task_ReviewFindings and before Task_RecordDecision: the findings are the evidence, so the options can only be weighed once they exist, and after Task_RecordDecision the decision is already written down. NOT between Gateway_EditorDecision and Task_RecordDecision, which is the pair the work-plan named — in this diagram those run the OTHER WAY ROUND. Flow_21b goes Task_RecordDecision -> Gateway_EditorDecision, so the gateway reads a decision that has already been recorded, and interposing there would analyse options after the choice was made. In the Agent lane, and this diagram makes the reason sharp. Task_RecordDecision is a userTask in Lane_Editor that already names decision-audit, and Process_OptionsAnalysis ends with its own decision-audit note. Those are two different acts — the subprocess records that the options were WEIGHED, the editor records WHAT WAS CHOSEN — and putting the analysis in the editor's lane would collapse them, making the same party both analyse and decide. The subprocess's own documentation refuses that: it produces options and a recommendation, and the authorisation belongs to the calling step. CallActivity_Evidence sits in Lane_Editor instead, and that is not an inconsistency: the author performs the evidence retrieval, whereas here the point is that the analyst is not the decider. On the trigger: A_Frame opens the subprocess on opening-brief's trigger — irreversibility and surprise — and leaving there is a correct outcome. A spelling fix that reached Task_ReviewFindings with one mechanical finding exits immediately; a revise-or-discard on a block other content depends on does not. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/editing-hci-validation.bpmn#Call_OptionsAnalysis . Options analysis adopt · hold · decline candidate, extracted On the single edge into PM_Decide, and deliberately not earlier: the MVP build and its gates are HOW the options' costs are measured, so an analysis before Task_Mvp would weigh alternatives against no evidence. Everything the decider needs exists by the time the reviewer has finished and the fixable findings are fixed. In the Agent lane, because this step produces the analysis and does not make the decision — PM_Decide is a userTask whose lane admits person only, and putting the analysis in the agent's lane is what keeps that separation legible rather than implied. A subprocess that decided would be a second accepting party. Reached through the loop as well as straight through: SF_UA_8 re-enters at A_Impact, so a run where the reviewer found something fixable arrives here a second time with different evidence. That is a genuine re-analysis and its op="note" appends rather than deduping, which is the behaviour wanted — a second note records that the options were weighed again against changed inputs. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/upstream-version-adoption.bpmn#Call_OptionsAnalysis . Options analysis how to absorb the impact candidate, extracted On the edge OUT of Task_AssessImpact and before Task_CommitPush, because the impact assessment is the evidence the options are weighed against. An analysis before it would compare ways of absorbing a downstream effect nobody has measured yet; one after the commit would be a rationalisation of a choice already pushed. NOT between Task_AssessImpact and Task_ReviewImpact, although that is the handoff the work-plan named. Those two tasks are in DIFFERENT LANES with no sequence flow between them — the agent's assessment reaches the committee through Task_CompareBeforeAfter, not directly — so there was no edge there to interpose on. The conceptual handoff is real; the edge was not. In the Agent lane, matching upstream-version-adoption: this step produces the options and their trade-offs, and GW_Approved in the Review Committee lane is where a decision is taken. A subprocess in the reviewer's lane would read as the committee analysing its own options, which is a different process. On the trigger: reaching this call is not the same as running the whole of it. Process_OptionsAnalysis opens with A_Frame, whose trigger is opening-brief's — irreversibility and surprise, not size — and leaving at that first activity is a correct outcome rather than a skipped step. A copy-edit exits immediately; a logic change that moves an indicator does not, and this is the diagram where that distinction has teeth, since Task_EditLogic feeds straight into the assessment. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/content-change-review.bpmn#Call_OptionsAnalysis . Options analysis how to implement candidate, extracted On the single edge from Start_Process_CRDM_Deliver into A_Implement, so the approach is chosen before any code exists. By Phase 6 the needs, requirements and data model are signed off, which is exactly the evidence an options analysis needs and the reason it belongs here rather than earlier: at Call_Needs there is nothing to weigh, and after A_Implement the choice has been made in code. Note where this is NOT. The work-plan named crdm-requirements-workflow, and A_Implement is not in that diagram — crdm-requirements.bpmn is the orchestrator, seven call activities and a gateway, and Phase 6 lives here in crdm-deliver.bpmn. The call goes where the step is, not where the plan said to look. The three loop-backs into A_Implement — _5 (increment rejected), _7 (MVP not ready), _13 (feedback translated) — deliberately BYPASS this call. Routing them through it would run the subprocess on every iteration of the inner loop, which is the ceremony this design refuses: a gate invoked on every pass stops being read. An iteration reworks an approach already chosen; if the APPROACH is what is wrong, that is not a loop iteration and it belongs to the calling step in crdm-requirements.bpmn. Contrast upstream-version-adoption, where the loop DOES re-enter the analysis. There the loop-back returns to A_Impact, which re-gathers the evidence, so the second pass weighs genuinely different inputs. Here the loop returns to implementation with the evidence unchanged. A_Implement carries cat-harness.processes:bean op="claim"; this step carries no bean op, because Process_OptionsAnalysis ends with its own decision-audit note on the bean the caller claimed. Place it in uploads/ by a declared route [upload-routes] candidate, extracted THE FIRST LINK, and it did not exist until 2026-09-30. Everything downstream of here takes a file that is already in the queue: document-intake triggers on "User drops a file into uploads/", and both ingest Tools type their first input as "The upload to ingest, under the declared uploads graph". So the act of PUTTING it there was performed by three different mechanisms and governed by none of them. WHAT THIS STEP IS. Choosing an arrival route, writing the bytes into the declared queue of the instance that will own them, and discharging what that route does not discharge for you. The routes, what each writer owes, and the two that are mechanisms against the one that is a persona are in the upload-routes skill; upload-url composes the forge URL for the web route from the declaration rather than from a literal, because a hand-written one 404'd. WHY A PLAIN bpmn:task AND NOT A userTask. A userTask asserts a human performs it, and this lane is named "Contributor (human or agent)" precisely because both do — measured over this repository's own history, files have reached uploads/ in commits authored by Carl Leitner and in commits authored by Claude. Asserting human-only here would be the activity-fulfilment-kind contradiction written deliberately: the diagram saying one thing and the lane's role graph another. A plain task asserts nothing about the performer, which is the truth. WHY THE BEAN OP IS note AND NOT claim. Placing a file claims nothing; it adds to a queue. What it owes the work plan is visibility — three batches of PDFs arrived through the forge's web UI (c8349950fa5, f4ddfc65c8d, b8549160bb1) with no bean, no PR and no note, and the first sibling to notice was a generator going stale. A note against the ingestion bean is what makes the queue's growth something another session can see. A re-ingested document whose text changed re-enters it on its own, because the record's source_hash no longer matches. What an agent doing ingestion work does here is DRAIN a few: bun run summaries:next -- --n K hands it the next K blocks with their text, it writes a short summary of each in its own words, and bun run summaries:record writes them into library/<bib-slug>/summaries.json as drafts naming the agent and its model. The only job here holding contents: write, which is also how bun run gates knows not to run it locally. Process_RenderKgToCdn, entered with the tree this build already rendered and verified, the site root as the publication root URL, and GitHub Pages as the target — so its gh-pages Tool pushes. Here that push is a FULL REPLACE of the gh-pages branch: anything on it this build did not produce is gone unless the restore put it back, which is why the restore and the survival check either side of this call stay in THIS process rather than in the general one. The call returns the push's status and message (the gh-pages merge commit and the QA result); a status other than pushed takes the no branch of Did the deploy succeed?. Push to the CDN at STAGING/&lt;slug&gt;/ [render-kg-to-cdn] candidate, extracted A PREVIEW IS THE GENERAL STEP WITH A DIFFERENT ROOT (owner, 2026-09-30: "independent of staging vs publication … just rendering"). Process_RenderKgToCdn, entered with the tree Task_Build rendered, STAGING/<slug>/ under the site root as the publication root URL, and GitHub Pages as the target, so its gh-pages Tool pushes. For this target the push is keep_files: true with a destination_dir, so it adds one directory beside whatever else is on the branch; it is also RETRIED once: five other workflows push to gh-pages without joining this one's concurrency group, and a queue does not help because GitHub CANCELS a pending job when a newer one arrives for the same group rather than queueing it. Measured 2026-09-19: three staging runs from three different branches inside 17 seconds, two cancelled. The call returns the push's status and message; the render log and the PR comment that follow are this process's own. THE PREVIEW CAP rides in the same commit (owner ruling 2026-10-02, issue #1868: "cap the maximum number of previews (<= 10) and rotate old ones off", amended 2026-10-04 to a SIZE budget: "Cap by size, not count", "3gb"): staging-rotate.ts keeps this preview plus the most recently updated others while their total fits MAX_PREVIEW_BYTES = 3 GB and removes the rest, oldest first, each with a removed render-log entry and its record retired into STAGING/_retired/. Every push attempt re-reads gh-pages and re-decides rather than rebasing, so a lost race never pushes a stale removal. A rotated-off preview is regenerated by the next push to its PR branch. Re-materialize, re-asking the five gates — and record the new fixity candidate, extracted The gates are re-asked, not inherited: a licence can change, and a collection can grow past the size a caller agreed to. AND THE NEW FIXITY IS RECORDED IN THE SAME CHANGE. This step rewrites bytes that a materialization record describes, so leaving the old digest behind would make a CORRECT run of this process fail check:materialized-fixity as a mismatch — the gate reading "somebody edited held content without saying so" about the one process whose job is to replace it. Measured 2026-09-22 (bean 10s1): this task named no fixity write at all. This is the owner's publication exception, stated as a rule rather than as a carve-out. The exception is NOT "these actors may skip the rule"; it is "say what you did". A writer that updates the digest alongside the bytes passes, and the record then describes what is actually there. A writer that does not fails, correctly, because it has forked upstream silently. A list of permitted writers would go stale the first time somebody added a sixth one; this does not. For a false claim, check the checker's reading before trusting it. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/narrative-code-review.bpmn#A_ReRead . Tools: merge:overlap for the overlap facts, check:head-has-run for ownCi. Nothing read here is written to a queue entry; it is the input to the placement table. ownCi IS NOT A VERDICT READ. Never ask whether anything is red: ask which workflow runs are OWED for the head's event and whether each one is present and successful. The two readings come apart, measured 2026-10-02 on #1889's head 7ab6119405 -- 9 runs present, all 9 gating job NAMES matching, 3 of them in_progress with a null conclusion, and 3 check SUITES completed as action_required having executed nothing. A filter for conclusion = failure finds zero, and counting the runs does not catch it either. check:head-has-run is the only thing here that asks the owed question (bean 3pqn), and the five states it distinguishes are the five values of ownCi. Rule_HeadNotGreen in merge-priority.dmn then hands back anything but green, so this is a gate the engine applies rather than advice a steward remembers. Overlap kind matters as much as overlap: merge:overlap over all 36 open PRs on 2026-10-02 (459 pairs) found #1907 x #1909 NOT independent on package.json alone, with zero authored content shared. generated-only needs a regeneration and shared-declaration needs ordering; only authored needs a train.
