Never read source off the declaration directly — the config override and the legacy storage field are folded in by the resolver and nowhere else. A contradiction (both source and storage; a qa subgraph keyed by tip) throws here, before anything is mounted. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/mount-subgraph.bpmn#Task_ResolveSource . Resolve the Subgraphs and the root URL candidate, extracted Read the instance's declaration. Every Subgraph id asked for must be one it declares; none asked for means the whole graph. The root URL is the one given, else the declaration's iriBase, else https://<owner>.github.io/<repo>/. An unknown id is refused, never rendered as a smaller site. BPMN activities of bootstrap-tools · source bootstrap-tools/processes/render-kg-to-github-pages.bpmn#A_ResolveInputs . Resolve the Subgraphs, the root URL and the target's Tool candidate, extracted Every Subgraph id asked for must be one the declaration lists; none means the whole graph. The root URL is the one given. The target's Tool is the one that satisfies: ["render-kg-to-cdn"] for that CDN — gh-pages for GitHub Pages. A caller that already rendered and verified its tree hands the tree over instead of the graph, and the Tool pushes it without rendering again. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/render-kg-to-cdn.bpmn#Task_Resolve . Restore derived state [ig-publication] candidate, extracted ig-cache restore: per-artefact records, the terminology cache, the package cache and temp/, keyed by the toolchain slug. Exit 0 usable, 1 miss, 2 environment error, 3 present but toolchain moved. BPMN activities of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/processes/content/ig-incremental-build.bpmn#Task_Restore . Restore the OPEN PRs' staging previews candidate, extracted Copy every OPEN pull request's STAGING/<slug>/ preview from gh-pages into the publish directory before the replace, once per publish attempt. Without it the full replace deletes every preview, silently (bean plj1). Only open PRs' previews are carried. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/docs-site-publish.bpmn#Task_Restore . Restricted checkout of the backward cone candidate, extracted git sparse-checkout of the cone's files plus sushi-config.yaml, ig.ini and the alias files — a median of three files, p90 eleven, on smart-immunizations. BPMN activities of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/processes/content/ig-incremental-build.bpmn#Task_Checkout . RESTRICTIONS unknown is an answer, not a green light candidate, extracted The owner's phrase is 'no restrictions known in context', and that is a STATE, not a green light. GateVerdict is three-valued for this reason alone, and unknown is never rendered as permitted. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/materialize-remote.bpmn#Task_Restrictions . RETENTION what expires this copy candidate, extracted A copy with no expiry cannot be told from an abandoned one — the same argument bean-blocking makes about a block with no expiry. An ARCHIVAL copy is the exception and it is a specification rather than an omission: freshness() reports it permanent, not no-expiry. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/materialize-remote.bpmn#Task_Retention . Retire an actor — never delete one candidate, extracted An actor id is referenced from roles, diagrams, beans and commits, so removing the file leaves every one of those unable to tell retirement from accident. Same rule, and the same reason, as a scrapped bean. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/actor-role-administration.bpmn#Task_RetireActor . Retire or archive [content-retire] candidate, extracted No more content is planned: deprecate the folio. Post a deprecation notice and timeline, update its status metadata, archive it, point references at any successor, and remove it from active publication. The programme manager decides; retirement archives rather than deletes. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/content-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_Retire . Retrieve for each sub-question candidate, extracted The paper's Searcher, at the granularity A_Plan chose. Which retrieval paradigm — text-only, vision-only or hybrid — is recorded in the methodology node as an open trade-off rather than settled here: the paper's comparison was measured on its own corpus and says nothing about a folio's. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/library/deep-document-research.bpmn#A_Search . Retry a declared-flaky gate once candidate, extracted T7, narrow (R11; TAP17 Table II p. 5): only gates on a declared flaky list (browser e2e), once, both outcomes recorded. A deterministic gate is never retried: that would spend a CI cycle to learn nothing. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/merge-train.bpmn#Task_RetryFlaky . Return for correction with annotations candidate, extracted The reviewer annotates specific passages that need correction and returns to the translator with detailed feedback. Each annotation includes: - The passage in question - What is wrong (terminology, meaning, style) - The suggested correction or reference . BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/human-translation-workflow.bpmn#Task_ReturnForCorrection . Review each slice [review-task] candidate, extracted review-task.bpmn, once per slice, in parallel lanes by role. What kind of thing changed decides which review the slice descends into; the reviewer takes on that inner lane's role for the call only. Each reviewer gives the slice's blocks a verdict, and comments on the pull request with the block: tag where something needs saying. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/content-change-review.bpmn#Call_ReviewSlices . Review impact assessment candidate, extracted Committee reviews the agent's impact assessment: - Were all downstream effects identified? - Are the indicator changes acceptable? - Does the logic change match the narrative intent? . BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/content-change-review.bpmn#Task_ReviewImpact . Review increment (test behaviour) candidate, extracted Inner loop: the BA tests each delivered increment against the acceptance criteria. They do not review code — they test behaviour. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-deliver.bpmn#BA_ReviewIncrement . Review requirements and impact analysis candidate, extracted The BA reviews the formal requirements and the impact analysis the agent produced. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-requirements-definition.bpmn#BA_ReviewReqs . Review staged rendering candidate, extracted Author reviews the rendered feature branch at <pages-url>/STAGING/<branch-slug>/ and compares against the main site. The staging banner shows the commit SHA. The agent's before/after preview (skill before-after-preview) sits beside the URLs, with its counts and status line. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/content-change-review.bpmn#Task_ReviewStaging . Review synthesised needs statement candidate, extracted The BA reviews what the agent synthesised and checks it against what they actually need. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-needs.bpmn#BA_ReviewNeeds . Review the adoption candidate, extracted The asset carries no description. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/methodology-from-source.bpmn#O_Review . Review the change candidate, extracted A human or an agent acting AS reviewer. Nothing is a reviewer; somebody acts as one for the duration of this lane. For a rendered change the reviewer reads the agent's before/after preview rather than building one. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/code-change-review.bpmn#Task_Review . Review the change set on its staging preview candidate, extracted The existing content-change review, unchanged, of the author's branch: its PR lists the PC refs it answers, and its staging preview is the after side of every deep link. A change the reviewers send back returns to the author inside that process. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/public-comment.bpmn#CallActivity_ChangeSet . Review the draft publication [content-review] candidate, extracted Content reviewer, QC reviewer and technical officer review the draft as a whole — coherence, phase-gate criteria, breaking vs non-breaking change. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/draft-to-publication.bpmn#Task_ReviewDraft . Review the editorial dependencies candidate, extracted uses[] is what a READER must have read to follow the block — never populated from the formal dependency graph. Once every changed block is covered, the committee checks the editorial dependencies of the change as a whole before judging its impact. Moved here from the harness's review-narrative by placement PR3 (bean 63wl): reading order is a property of folio content, so the step belongs to the content process, which reaches the harness's review by calling DOWN into review-task. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/content-change-review.bpmn#Task_ReviewUses . Review the findings candidate, extracted THE GATE: the editor sees every finding BEFORE anything reaches the corpus. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/editing-hci-validation.bpmn#Task_ReviewFindings . Review the guidance already in this content [content-review] candidate, extracted The author reads what the document, DAK or IG ALREADY says on this question, before looking outward. A recommendation that contradicts a sibling recommendation in the same artefact is a defect no external evidence will reveal. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/evidence-retrieval.bpmn#Task_ReviewExisting . Review the MVP against what we bind to candidate, extracted A narrower question than "is the new version good": does everything in binds still hold, checked against the deployed page. A userTask, and the lane admits person and agent — a review agent is a legitimate reviewer here, and the separation that matters is the next lane's: a reviewer cannot accept. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/upstream-version-adoption.bpmn#R_Review . Review the schema definition node candidate, extracted Does the node declare what KIND of node it is? Does a widened type carry its mirrors? Does a removed field leave a reason behind, so the next author does not re-add it in good faith? And where the node RENDERS to something the site serves — a colour, a glyph, a theme's tokens — does a Tool maintain that artefact, and does the visual fact have only one home? The node decides; the stylesheet reports. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/review-code.bpmn#Task_ReviewSchema . Review the Tool node candidate, extracted Does it name skills, and do they resolve? Is the mechanism it advertises the one that actually runs? Are its IRIs minted rather than written out? And the question a covered skill hides: is the COMMAND reachable, or only the skill satisfied? A skill can be served by the neighbours of its mechanism while the mechanism itself is reachable from no node, and check:tools reports it as covered and is right to. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/review-code.bpmn#Task_ReviewTool . Review the translation candidate, extracted Coverage, preserved terms and echoes are mechanical. A semantic round trip needs a back-translator that has not seen the original; where none has run, the criterion carries no verdict and that is the honest state. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/content/review-narrative.bpmn#Task_ReviewTranslation . Review translation for accuracy candidate, extracted A subject-matter expert reviews the injected translated markdown for: - Clinical/technical accuracy of terminology - Preservation of meaning from the source - Cultural appropriateness for the target locale - Consistency with the domain glossary For WHO content: the SME verifies that normative statements ("SHALL", "SHOULD", "MAY") are translated with the correct force in the target language. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/human-translation-workflow.bpmn#Task_SMEReview . Review what the substrate offers candidate, extracted Every subgraph, asset class and harness the cached declaration names, each with its current state — referenced, materialised, unknown, stale, or refused by a gate. Shown whole, because a reader who sees only what was chosen cannot tell "not offered" from "not taken". BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/subscribe-kg.bpmn#Task_Review . Revise the proposed change [content-author] candidate, extracted The editor chose revise: rework the proposed change against the findings the editor reviewed, then send it back through validation as a new proposal. The before/after preview is refreshed with it (skill before-after-preview). BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/editing-hci-validation.bpmn#Task_ReviseEdit . Root-cause the failure candidate, extracted "Flake" is not a root cause. A red PR is work now, whatever its review state — only a green, mergeable head waits on reviewers. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/code-change-review.bpmn#Task_Diagnose . Round-trip translation QA candidate, extracted Bean: folio-assistant-ktt2 Back-translates target-language .md to source language and compares meaning. Distinguishes semantic drift from terminology misses. Tool: translation_validate MCP tool No gateway follows: drift or clean, the translation goes to Task_SMEReview with the findings attached. Which of two readings is right is a human call (translation-manager, "route drift to a human reviewer"), and every translation in this workflow is reviewed and signed off anyway, so a clean result is evidence for the reviewer and never a way around them. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/human-translation-workflow.bpmn#Task_RoundTripQA . Round-trip translation QA candidate, extracted NOT IMPLEMENTED. Tracked as a bean; see docs/document-ingestion.md. Back-translate each localized narrative into its source language and compare meaning, to catch semantic drift and bad terminology that a forward-only check cannot see. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/ingest-l1-completeness-gate.bpmn#Task_RoundTrip . Round-trip translation QA (back-translate) candidate, extracted Bean: folio-assistant-ktt2 Back-translates the target-language .md into the source language and compares meaning with the original. Detects semantic drift and terminology misses that a forward-only fluency check cannot see. Tool: translation_validate MCP tool . BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/translation-workflow.bpmn#Task_RoundTripQA . Route it, and watch the queue candidate, extracted A file goes to ingestion; a link or a description goes to whatever will resolve it. Acquisition stops here — the moment a file is in the queue, library-ingestion owns it, and keeping that seam sharp is what lets a resource acquired through a channel that does not exist yet reach ingestion unchanged. An arrival may be minutes or days away, so it is watched rather than chased. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/content-acquisition.bpmn#A_Route . Run check:ci-health, WRITING the report file candidate, extracted Run check:ci-health --out, writing the report file before any exit path. Exit 0 clean, 1 live failures, 2 could not check. bun also exits 1 on an uncaught exception, so an exit 1 with no report file is a crash and is treated as could-not-check. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/ci-health-watch.bpmn#Task_Check . Run every verifier over the export candidate, extracted Run the verifier set (scripts/publish-verify.ts, bun run publish:verify -- --dir <site>) over the built tree. A SET: each verifier is one entry, and adding one changes nothing else. The first is JSON-LD expansion under a real processor, network refused — a property the context does not declare, a relative IRI or a context that will not load is a finding. Only documents of OURS are verified; third-party data in the tree is counted and cannot block. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/publish-verification.bpmn#A_Verify . Run placement, and raise a bean for the authoring candidate, extracted The offer produces a DECISION, not a node. placement then decides instance, graph and node kind — it is the step that catches a hardcoded path or a literal naming one folio — and the authoring itself becomes a bean, because work here is a bean before it is a file. op="note" and not create, for the reason A_CreateBeans above states: the engine has no create op — it claims, notes and resolves the instance's OWN bean. The agent mints the authoring bean itself with beans create, running the exact-title existence check first, and what this step records is a note that the decision was taken. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-signoff.bpmn#A_RecordKg . Run publication QA gates [content-test] candidate, extracted Publication-readiness QA across layers — QC reports, IG Publisher QA, proof status, broken links, build warnings. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/draft-to-publication.bpmn#Task_PublicationQa . Run the gate set on the train [code-quality-gates] candidate, extracted Every gate CI runs, on the combination (R2): a member that passes alone can still break main with another. The merge-gate epic (nok9, #1887) adds its gates here when they land. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/merge-train.bpmn#Call_Gates . Run the gates against the merge of head into base candidate, extracted CI tests the MERGE, not the branch. That is why a locally green tree can go red here: the agent's tree and the merge result are different trees, and the difference is invisible from a checkout. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/code-change-review.bpmn#Task_RunCI . Run the health checks, keeping the report either way candidate, extracted Run bun run health --out and upload the JSON report whatever the verdict — on unknown it is the only evidence of why the sweep went blind. Exit 0 clean, 1 gating findings, 2 could not check; exit 1 with no report is a crash. The checks report and never act: every finding names something a person does. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/repository-health-watch.bpmn#Task_Check . Run the node audits candidate, extracted check:tools, kg:audit and typecheck. Read the kg-qa sidecar rather than the summary: it is written per node so an inherited defect and a new one are distinguishable. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/review-code.bpmn#Task_RunNodeAudits . Run the platform's own gates candidate, extracted Before pushing, not after CI says so. bun test passing is NOT the gates passing: measured 2026-09-19, a green unit suite sat beside a tsc failure and a missing @graphNode tag, and the second broke a QA sidecar comparison as well — one cause, two symptoms, and an agent running only the tests would have pushed all three. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/code-change-review.bpmn#Task_RunGates . Run the row's gates tests · e2e · site-links candidate, extracted The mvp commands declared for this tenant. For the theme: bun test, CI=1 bunx playwright test (a11y, action tiles, sidebar panels, QA panel) and scripts/site-links.ts --site ./_site, which checks the navbar tiles against the BUILT site rather than against the attribute — the distinction that let a 404 ship unnoticed once already. A red gate is EVIDENCE, not an exit. It does not end the process and it does not loop by itself: "this version breaks us" is a finding the decider needs, not a reason to stop before they see it. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/upstream-version-adoption.bpmn#Task_Gates . Run the rule's mechanical half candidate, extracted Whatever patterns and terminology the rule carries. A judgementOnly rule has no mechanical half by declaration, which is different from nobody having written one yet. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/content/voice-review.bpmn#Task_MechanicalHalf .

12483.title: S
12483.content: Say it could not be confirmed candidate, extracted No URL, no probe, or a failed request. Reported as "could not check", never as "not yet" and never as "live". BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/conduct/getting-started.bpmn#Task_ReportUnknown . Say what is being decided, and why it matters now candidate, extracted First, and in the message itself: where you are (the Process and task, as which Role, asking whom — from the three determinations), what the decision is, what depends on it, and what is already known — each fact with where it came from. A link is where somebody goes for more; it is never where the terms are defined. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/human-agent-discussion.bpmn#A_GiveContext . Say what is needed, and ask for a link OR a description candidate, extracted Both forms, named together. A person who cannot find the file often knows exactly what it is, and a description in their own words is an acquired resource rather than a consolation prize. Asking for the upload first demands the one thing they may not have, before the cheaper answers have been offered. Say what happens if they do nothing. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/content-acquisition.bpmn#A_Ask . Say what moved and where it went candidate, extracted Tell the reader what moved and where it went, so the content can be found in the trashcan rather than inferred missing from a card that disappeared. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/ui/board-relocate.bpmn#A_ReportMove . Say where it will be candidate, extracted A measured 404. The author is told the address and that the first build has not landed there yet — which is useful, and is not the same as being told it is live. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/conduct/getting-started.bpmn#Task_ReportPending . Scaffold the folio (folio_init) candidate, extracted content/, uploads/, library/, the first manifests, <slug>.json and <slug>.config.json, the builder shim, AGENTS.md with its stubs, .mcp.json, the session-start hook and the beans store. Refuses rather than overwrites when a folio is already present. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/conduct/getting-started.bpmn#Task_Scaffold . Scan open issues for match candidate, extracted Search open issues, then recently closed ones, by title and body keywords for one this request belongs to. Requirements may span several issues; note every relevant one. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-issue-linking.bpmn#A_ScanIssues . Scan the environment opportunities and threats candidate, extracted The external axis, first, per Weihrich. Work the source's categories of environmental change rather than free-associating: societal, governmental, economic, competitive, supplier and market changes, each item recorded with what it impacts. An opportunity is an external element that gives benefit; a threat is one that could cause trouble. Both are outside the subject and largely beyond its control — that is what puts them on this axis, not whether they feel good or bad. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/swot-analysis.bpmn#A_ScanExternal . Scan the repo for content worth importing candidate, extracted Read-only. Classifies candidates into library/ (external source) and content/ (authored here), and reports what it could not classify as its own bucket rather than forcing every file into one of the two. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/conduct/getting-started.bpmn#Task_ScanRepo . Scan the subject strengths and weaknesses candidate, extracted The internal axis. Work the source's functional checklist rather than a blank page: marketing, research and development, management information systems, management team, operations, finance, human resources. A strength gives advantage over others in the field; a weakness places the subject at a disadvantage relative to others. Both are attributes OF the subject. The source's warning belongs to this step specifically: listing strengths on paper "is very different from testing the organization and experiencing the strengths at work", so a strength recorded here is a claim, and where evidence for it exists it is cited. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/swot-analysis.bpmn#A_ScanInternal . Schema and constraint checks [content-validate] candidate, extracted Block schema, label prefixes, required fields, constraint rules. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/editing-hci-validation.bpmn#Task_SchemaValidate . Scope the criterion so it stops applying here candidate, extracted One edit to the criterion rather than ten overrules on the blocks it should never have covered. This branch is the one an adjudicator under time pressure converts into a dispensation, and the conversion is a defect: a dispensation lapses when the source moves, so a mis-scoped criterion granted its way past comes back every time anybody touches the block. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/criterion-adjudication.bpmn#A_ScopeCriterion . Scope the DAK [content-plan] candidate, extracted Enumerate the processes, decisions and data elements the guideline implies; identify the actors. BPMN activities of smart-base · source smart-base/processes/content/l2-dak-authoring.bpmn#Task_ScopeDak . Scope the delta pinned → candidate candidate, extracted Restricted to the directories that reach our output — for a Jekyll theme _sass, _includes, _layouts, assets. Upstream's own docs, CI and tests cannot reach us, and counting them makes a harmless release look alarming. The changelog is the claim; git diff --stat pinned..candidate over those paths is the evidence. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/upstream-version-adoption.bpmn#A_Scope . Scope the sample: which items, which store, and is it PERMANENT? candidate, extracted Three answers, recorded before anything is fetched. WHICH ITEMS: named by the source's identifiers, or by a subset strategy its descriptor supports. WHICH STORE: the knowledge graph or other structured store the import is tested against. PERMANENT OR TRIAL: a permanent sample lands in library/ and is refreshed; a trial lands in fsh-guts/ and is not. The purpose materialize-remote asks for (working or archival) is asked there, not here. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/sample-import.bpmn#Task_Scope . Scrap the bean, with the reason candidate, extracted The agent's own beans update --status scrapped; never deleted. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/merge-refusal.bpmn#Task_Scrap . Scrap with reasons NEVER delete candidate, extracted status: scrapped, plus a "Reasons for Scrapping" section. This is what "disable" means here — the CLI has no disabled state; its vocabulary is draft, todo, in-progress, completed, scrapped. DELETION IS NEVER THE ANSWER, even though beans delete exists. A scrapped bean records that the work was considered and rejected, and why; a deleted one leaves a sibling session unable to tell abandonment from accident, and leaves the next agent free to re-open the same dead end. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/bean-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_Scrap . Search beans for relevance candidate, extracted beans list --json / beans query over titles AND bodies, open and recently completed. A completed bean is evidence of a decision already made. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/related-work.bpmn#A_SearchBeans . Search issues and open PRs candidate, extracted The repository's issues (open and closed) and its open pull requests. An open PR touching the same files is the collision most worth finding early. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/related-work.bpmn#A_SearchIssues . Search the published slice in a browser candidate, extracted Open slices/search.html?slice=<name> on the deployed site, run a phrase search for a known row, open it so its payload is fetched, and look at the result; send the screenshot rather than a description of it. Report the mode the page says it used (OPFS or in memory), never an assumed one. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/slice-sqlite-publish.bpmn#A_Verify . Search trusted CONTENT — L2 DAKs, L3 IGs candidate, extracted Already-adjudicated guidance: WHO SMART DAKs at L2 and FHIR Implementation Guides at L3. A recommendation adopted in a published DAK is evidence of a different kind from a primary study -- it is a prior decision, with its own provenance, and must be cited as that rather than laundered into primary evidence. NOT YET SKILL-BACKED. This step named corpus-search, which has never existed. It is not corpus-grep, whose job is the pre-declaration check that something really is an open gap — searching adjudicated L2/L3 content for evidence is a different task, so pointing the ref there would have been a plausible-looking wrong answer. Left uncovered until the skill is written. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/evidence-retrieval.bpmn#Task_L2L3Content . Search trusted SOURCES — L1 [document-intake] candidate, extracted Ingested primary literature under library/: the sections/*.md tree and, where a document was scanned, ocr/page-NNN.txt. NOTE the known blind spot — a document OCR'd but never re-run through pdf-structure.py has only a stub in sections/, so a sections-only search misses it. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/evidence-retrieval.bpmn#Task_L1Sources . Two schemes with different properties remain to choose between, and the trustlist does not choose between them. A PACKAGE signature over the manifest verifies the SET — nothing added, removed or altered — and must be reissued whenever any file changes. A PER-ASSET signature verifies one file independently, which is what an edge cache serving one asset can actually check, and it cannot detect a removal because there is nothing left to verify. 12526.title: Authored terms
12526.content: Bootstrap terms . The terms Bootstrap defines, in order: each is defined only by terms above it, and never itself. Read from the schema that defines them, bootstrap/schemas/graph.schema.json, so this glossary cannot say anything that schema does not. SKOS. 1. Node One file, or one part of a file addressable by an IRI fragment, named by an IRI. Bootstrap terms · https://litlfred.github.io/bootstrap/0.1.0/ns#Node · defined by www.w3.org/TR/json-ld11/#node-objects · source bootstrap/schemas/graph.schema.json#/$defs/Node . 2. Reference A Node's naming of another Node by its IRI. Uses: Node . Bootstrap terms · https://litlfred.github.io/bootstrap/0.1.0/ns#Reference · defined by www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3987 · source bootstrap/schemas/graph.schema.json#/$defs/Reference . 3. Node Schema A schema a Node can be checked against: a JSON Schema, or a published external schema such as BPMN's. Uses: Node . Bootstrap terms · https://litlfred.github.io/bootstrap/0.1.0/ns#NodeSchema · defined by json-schema.org/draft-07/schema# · source bootstrap/schemas/graph.schema.json#/$defs/NodeSchema . 4. Node Kind A name paired with a Node Schema. Uses: Node Schema . Bootstrap terms · https://litlfred.github.io/bootstrap/0.1.0/ns#NodeKind · defined by litlfred.github.io/bootstrap/0.1.0/schemas/graph.schema.json#/properties/nodeSchemas · source bootstrap/schemas/graph.schema.json#/$defs/NodeKind . 5. Subkind A Node Kind whose Node Schema requires everything another Node Kind's does, so every Node that satisfies it satisfies the other too. Uses: Node Kind, Node Schema, Node . Bootstrap terms · https://litlfred.github.io/bootstrap/0.1.0/ns#Subkind · defined by litlfred.github.io/bootstrap/0.1.0/schemas/graph.schema.json#/$defs/Subkind · source bootstrap/schemas/graph.schema.json#/$defs/Subkind . 6. Node Instance A Node that names its Node Kind, in $schema or front matter, and satisfies that kind's Node Schema. Uses: Node, Node Kind, Node Schema . Bootstrap terms · https://litlfred.github.io/bootstrap/0.1.0/ns#NodeInstance · defined by litlfred.github.io/bootstrap/0.1.0/schemas/graph.schema.json#/$defs/NodeInstance · source bootstrap/schemas/graph.schema.json#/$defs/NodeInstance . 7. Graph Kind A named set of Node Kinds. Uses: Node Kind . Bootstrap terms · https://litlfred.github.io/bootstrap/0.1.0/ns#GraphKind · defined by litlfred.github.io/bootstrap/0.1.0/schemas/graph.schema.json#/$defs/GraphKind · source bootstrap/schemas/graph.schema.json#/$defs/GraphKind . 8. Extension A field of a Declaration, or of one of its entries, that is not defined here. A reader that does not recognise the field ignores it, and the rest of the Declaration keeps its meaning. Uses: Declaration . Bootstrap terms · https://litlfred.github.io/bootstrap/0.1.0/ns#Extension · defined by litlfred.github.io/bootstrap/0.1.0/schemas/graph.schema.json#/$defs/Extension · source bootstrap/schemas/graph.schema.json#/$defs/Extension . 10.
